sam_w: Hey—noticed tail latency bump on host-side for short calls after yesterday's kernel selection change. Profiling shows more syscalls and smaller writev coalesces.

maria_g: saw that. any relationship to batching hint change? we pushed heuristic to favor larger batches at ingress.

liam_h: yes, logs show batch sizes increased but per-request tokenization is now in host process instead of sidecar for small payloads => more fragmented writes. kv-cache hit rate dipped ~6%.

nina_m: attaching small snippet from perf: ```text
syscall_count: +28% (writev dominated)
avg_writev_size: 512 -> 208 bytes
kvcache_hit: 84% -> 78%
``` 

perfbot: perf alert created: #PR 4321 linked, baseline vs canary diffs summarized.

sam_w: proposal: revert kernel-picker change for quantized models (it picks avx2 path instead of int8 fast path for seq<64). Also consider coalescing small frame writes at proxy layer and re-evaluate batch-heuristic weight for short sequences.

maria_g: can we toggle kernel selector via env for canary? e.g., `REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=legacy_smallseq` — run 5% traffic.

liam_h: yep canary config ready. Also plan to gate tokenization move: keep small calls pre-tokenized at edge for now (`edge_tokenize=true`), that'll reduce host-side syscall churn.

nina_m: quick microbench command I ran: `wrk -c200 -d60 -s scripts/short_payload.lua` — with coalesce patch avg p50 drops 12ms.

sam_w: sounds good. action items:
- liam_h: launch kernel-selector canary (5%) and measure 95/99 latencies + kvcache hits
- maria_g: flip `edge_tokenize` flag in edge canary
- nina_m: prototype writev coalescer in proxy, push PR
- me: monitor perfbot and rollback thresholds

maria_g: ping @perfbot when canary is live so dashboards auto-annotate :thumbsup:

liam_h: launching canary now (pid 7832). will post followups in this thread.

perfbot: canary started: 5% traffic -> rollout id cr-2026-06-22-01

sam_w: thanks — let's aim to keep hosts from doing per-request small writes while we validate kernel selection. will update after first 10min checks.
